question: Who is an active listener?
expected_answer: Someone who listens attentively without interrupting the speaker

question: What is social injustice?
expected_answer: Unfair treatment of people who are marginalised
answer: Social injustice is the unfair treatment of people who are considered marginalised because they have traits different from the majority or are considered less privileged (GSCS S4, p. 17). It involves a collection of shared unjust experiences that affect a group of people who are seen as inferior (GSCS S4, p. 17). This group is expected to remain silent to the advantage of a dominant group, which makes interaction hard and hinders social cohesion (GSCS S4, p. 17).

question: What is the difference between leisure and sport?
expected_answer: Leisure is free time spent away from business, work, domestic chores and education
answer:
Leisure is free time spent away from business, work, domestic chores, and education, excluding necessary activities like eating and sleeping (GSCS S4, p. 33). It involves activities like entertaining friends, going on vacation, or doing hobbies (GSCS S4, p. 33). 

Sport involves all forms of competitive physical activities, through casual or organized participation, that aim to use, maintain, or improve physical ability and skills while providing entertainment (GSCS S4, p. 39).

question: What is the difference between oral and non-verbal communication?
expected_answer: Oral communication is verbal; non-verbal communication uses other means
answer:
Oral communication is communicated verbally using spoken words [GSCS S4, p. 43]. 

Non-verbal communication is communicated by other means instead of verbal words [GSCS S4, p. 43]. Examples of non-verbal communication include written and recorded messages, online information, expressions like gestures, tone of voice, touch, smell, body motion, and creative and aesthetic symbols [GSCS S4, p. 43]. Non-verbal communication also includes dancing, sculpturing, sign language, body language, body posture, and physical contact [GSCS S4, p. 44].
